impact_narrative: Checkout p99 is 2.4s against a 780ms baseline, burning the latency budget 6x, with no elevated error rate so far.
cause_summary: Latency is concentrated in the payment authorization path. A 250ms batching window, a shared HTTP client left on default pool limits, and doubled worker concurrency all plausibly contribute, and no deploy event landed in the window to separate them.

runbook_citation.heading_path: Checkout Service Runbook > Dashboards and logs
runbook_citation.why: Latency triage starts at the Checkout Overview dashboard and the payments provider view, since no single commit is implicated.

next_steps: Compare Checkout Overview latency percentiles against the payments provider dashboard to split gateway time from service time.
Check whether the p99 rise tracks the batching window by temporarily lowering it to 50ms.
If service time dominates, inspect connection pool saturation on the shared HTTP client.
